title: Virtual Head Attention: Shattering the LLM KV Cache Wall

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how Virtual Head Attention cuts 84.4% of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A VRAM bar filling up rapidly in red.

beats.text: Standard GQA forces a brutal trade-off: sacrifice accuracy or drown in cache overhead. It is an impossible triangle.
beats.visual_focus: A triangle diagram with vertices labeled Cache, Compute, and Quality.

beats.text: Virtual Head Attention shatters this by projecting heads into a latent space, then using a learned linear Premix.
beats.visual_focus: Animation showing high-dimensional heads collapsing into a compact latent space.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out the KV cache as a memory black hole is exactly the kind of pain point I actually care about. I didn't swipe because you got straight to the point. I got a bit lost on 'learned linear Premix'—is that a specific layer type or just a fancy way of saying a weight matrix? Other than that, the explanation of folding the operations into the projection matrices at inference made total sense. It sounds like a legit optimization rather than marketing fluff.
